grandparents_cupboard.reason: Ricotta, eggs, milk, flour, butter, honey, Greek yoghurt, lemon and grapes are all plain whole foods a grandparent could have kept.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including ricotta and red grapes, is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a small pan, a frying pan, a bowl and a whisk, and drop pancakes are within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: 150g self-raising flour with 250g ricotta, 3 eggs and 150ml milk gives a sound, thick batter for about 12–16 small pancakes, and 2 minutes a side over butter will cook them through, so four people are fed.

honest_times.reason: Halving 300g grapes, mixing the batter and frying several batches fits within 30 active minutes, and the 5-minute cook matches the grape warming.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the lemon (squeezed and zested), cinnamon and salt, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Warm honeyed grapes are named in the title and carry the dish, which suits a cool October morning.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or health preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Ricotta, eggs and Greek yoghurt give real protein alongside the fruit, making a proper family breakfast rather than a sugar hit.
